answer: Proof of Personhood protocols resist Sybil attacks by requiring cryptographic verification of a unique human link. An attacker faces the cost of securing biometric uniqueness, which is as difficult as navigating a glacier of entropy in a digital nebula. To harbor a vast army of fake agents, the adversary must exhaust unsustainable capital on identity validation, ensuring the integrity of the consensus network remains intact against mass-produced sub-identities.
